reports.text: Indication: headache, fever, neck stiffness; prior to lumbar puncture. Technique: axial noncontrast images of the head. Findings: No intracranial hemorrhage, mass, or mass effect. Ventricles and sulci are normal in size for age. Basal cisterns are patent. Gray-white differentiation preserved. No extra-axial collection. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear. Calvarium intact.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 01/12/2026 18:10. Discharged 01/13/2026 01:40.

CC: headache, light sensitivity, stiff neck, fever x2 days.

HPI: 19M, college student, mono last summer. Two days of headache with photophobia, neck stiffness and low fevers. More tired, nauseated, not eating much, aching all over. Several guys on his dorm floor had sore throats and felt run down over the past week. No travel, no animal contact, no drug use.

PMH: infectious mononucleosis 2025. Immunizations up to date per patient.
Meds: none.
Allergies: amoxicillin (rash).
FH: father HTN, mother hypothyroidism; no immunodeficiency or autoimmune disease.
SH: never smoker, occasional alcohol on weekends, lives in a residence hall.

Triage: T 38.1 C (100.6 F), BP 112/74, HR 92, RR 18.

Exam: awake and alert, uncomfortable, prefers the lights down. Photophobic. Nuchal rigidity present. Cranial nerves intact, strength and sensation symmetric, no focal deficit. No rash. Heart and lungs without abnormality.

ED course: CT head obtained before LP, unremarkable. LP L3-4 under sterile technique: clear fluid, opening pressure 170 mm H2O. CSF WBC 130/mm3 (92% lymphocytes), RBC 5/mm3, protein 76 mg/dL, glucose 64 mg/dL; serum glucose 98. Gram stain without organisms. CSF enterovirus PCR detected (resulted 23:30). Culture sent.

MDM: lymphocytic CSF with normal glucose ratio and no organisms on Gram stain, enterovirus PCR positive, well-appearing and nonfocal. Picture of viral meningitis; antibiotics not started. Felt better after rest and fluids, tolerating PO.

Diagnosis: enteroviral meningitis.
Disposition: home. Rest, fluids, OTC analgesics. Return for worsening headache, confusion, persistent vomiting, rash, or new weakness. PCP follow-up within 1-2 weeks.

Addendum 01/15/2026: CSF culture final, no growth.

[Received 02/09/2026 in response to records request.]

documents.title: ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I ended up in the ER last night with a horrible headache and stiff neck. they did a spinal tap and said it's viral meningitis, they said it was a virus that's going around the dorm. they sent me home at like 2am. head still hurts but better. they said to see my doctor

documents.title: RE: ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Asher, glad you got checked and that it looked viral. Viral meningitis usually clears on its own over a week or two. Rest, drink a lot, and use Tylenol or ibuprofen for the headache. If the headache gets much worse, you get confused, can't keep fluids down, or develop a rash or weakness, go back to the ED.

I'd like to see you next week. The front desk will call with a time.

events.reason: Follow-up after ED visit for meningitis

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-ED f/u. Seen 1/12 at an outside ED with 2 days of headache, photophobia, stiff neck and fever; several dormmates sick. Per pt: CT head normal, LP done, told viral, probably enterovirus, no antibiotics, home same night. ED records not here yet; request sent today.

Headache gone since about 1/17. No fevers. Appetite back. Still a little more tired than usual, missed most of the first week of classes, back now. No visual changes, no weakness, no numbness. Neck moves freely.

Also reports flu shot at the campus clinic mid-October, added.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Alert, conversational. Neck supple, no meningismus. PERRL, EOMI, no nystagmus. CN II-XII intact. Strength 5/5 throughout, reflexes 2+ and symmetric, gait normal. LP site clean, no tenderness.

A/P: Enteroviral meningitis, clinically resolved. Fatigue should continue to improve. Back to full activity as tolerated. Note given for missed classes. Call with any return of headache or fever.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Release signed. Request sent to outside ED for 01/12/2026 visit: physician note, CSF results, head CT report.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED record from 1/12 reviewed. CSF: OP 170, WBC 130 with 92% lymphs, protein 76, glucose 64 (serum 98), Gram stain negative, enterovirus PCR detected, culture no growth. Head CT normal. Consistent with what we discussed. Nothing further.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20 y/o here for yearly exam, finished freshman year, living at home for the summer.

Interval: mono last July (student health), recovered, LFTs normalized in August. Enteroviral meningitis in January (ED, CSF enterovirus PCR positive), fully recovered by our visit in late January. Since then no headaches, no illnesses. Energy back to normal.
Meds: none. Allergies: amoxicillin (rash).
SH: never smoker, no vaping. Alcohol stays occasional, 1-2 on a weekend. Sleep ok most of the time.
PHQ-9: 1.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well-appearing. Oropharynx clear, tonsils normal size. No cervical adenopathy. Heart without murmur, regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no liver or spleen felt. Skin clear. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
- Healthy young adult. Taking mono off the active problem list, long since resolved.
- Screening done in 2024, no labs needed this year.
- Vaccines: flu in the fall, campus or here. Otherwise current per records.
- See him over winter break or sooner as needed.
